sections.label: Productivity and median income growth
sections.summary: Labour productivity rose 2.7% per annum from 2016 to 2019, and real median income rose 3.7% per annum, both higher than the preceding three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Singapore's overall labour productivity, as measured by real value-added per actual hours worked, rose by 2.7% per annum from 2016 to 2019, up from 2.2% in the preceding three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Real median income from work of full-time Singaporeans, including employer CPF contributions, rose by 3.7% per annum from 2016 to 2019, higher than the 3.2% per annum growth in the preceding three years.

sections.label: Refreshing ITMs after COVID-19
sections.summary: COVID-19 accelerated structural trends, so the 23 ITM sectors' strategies will be updated to lift productivity and wages and create jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Beyond the immediate impact, COVID-19 has also accelerated long-term structural trends such as digital transformation, a review of globalisation and a focus on sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We must therefore build on the head-start and progress that we have made in the last five years, and refresh our ITMs to meet the accelerated changes brought about by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For each of the 23 ITM sectors, we will update our sectoral strategies to create and seize opportunities through digitalisation, innovation, internationalisation, upskilling of workers and job redesign, with the aim of lifting the productivity and wages of our workers, and creating good jobs for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Jobs Growth Incentive funding
sections.summary: Another $5.2 billion was allocated in the recent Budget to the Jobs Growth Incentive to extend the hiring window by seven months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: One example is the Jobs Growth Incentive, to which we have allocated another $5.2 billion during the recent Budget to extend the hiring window by seven months.

sections.label: Digitalisation progress among SMEs
sections.summary: Digital leaders and performers among SMEs rose from 9% to 12% from 2019 to 2020, and digital starters fell from 68% to 62%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: If you take, for example, the whole digitalisation trend, we are not waiting for the update of these ITMs before we act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We have increased the number of digital leaders and performers, especially among SMEs, from 9% to 12% from 2019 to 2020, and the share of digital starters also fell from 68% to 62%.

sections.label: Jobs Growth Incentive and SGUnited
sections.summary: The Jobs Growth Incentive incentivises companies that decide to grow to draw in more workers, which is what the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package is about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: To meet this job growth, the answer is not just in the Government deciding which are the sectors that will grow and which are the sectors that will not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And the significance of the Jobs Growth Incentive is exactly that when companies decide that they are going to grow, we incentivise them to draw in more workers and that is what the whole SGUnited Jobs and Skills package is all about.

sections.label: Linking ITM work to R&D
sections.summary: ITM work has been reorganised to link to R&D so technology and innovation can be worked on simultaneously, helping companies transform and workers gain skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Indeed, in fact, I have just made some changes in the way we organise our ITM work to link it to our work on R&D so that as technology and innovation play a more critical role in our economic future, we can work on both simultaneously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: How can we help companies to transform to be more technologically savvy?

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And, in turn, I mentioned about the jobs transformation programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: How do we design programmes to enable our workers to have better skills in order to access those better jobs so that not only do the companies have higher productivity but our workers can look forward to higher wages and better employment prospects?

sections.label: Pandemic lessons and vaccine production
sections.summary: Economic agencies are working on new vaccine production opportunities, with budgetary support provided to secure such projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Mr Sharael Taha mentioned about whether we should take into account the lessons learnt from the pandemic as well as the lessons from these few years of implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And to the Member's specific question, for example, on manufacturing, what are the new opportunities for production of vaccines, for example, or even some way in which we can play a role in the vaccine, the economic agencies have been working very hard on this and I would leave the economic agencies to provide the announcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: All I can say is that I have provided sufficient budgetary support for us to secure some of these projects.

sections.label: Work from home game-changer
sections.summary: The Member's view that work from home and anywhere is a game-changer is agreed, but it cuts both ways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As to the Member's second question about work from home and work from anywhere and that this is a game-changer, I fully agree with him that this is a game-changer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: But let me add that this is a game-changer that cuts both ways.
